{{short description|Austrian American mathematician (born 1969)}}
'''Wilhelm Schlag''' (born May 2, 1969) is a mathematician and Phillips Professor of Mathematics at [[Yale University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gauss.math.yale.edu/~ws442/|title=Wilhelm Schlag|website=math.yale.edu|access-date=2019-04-17}}</ref> He is known for his work in [[harmonic analysis]] and [[partial differential equations]].

== Career ==
Schlag obtained his PhD at the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1996 under the supervision of [[Thomas Wolff]]. Since then, he has held positions at [[Princeton University]], [[California Institute of Technology]] and the [[University of Chicago]] where he was H. J. Livingston Professor of Mathematics before moving to Yale University in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fas.yale.edu/book/new-faculty-2018-19/science/wilhelm-schlag|title=Wilhelm Schlag|website=fas.yale.edu|access-date=2019-04-29}}</ref> He has done extensive work in [[Fourier Analysis]], [[Spectral theory]] and [[Dispersive partial differential equation|dispersive]] partial differential equations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Wilhelm%20Schlag%22|title=Wilhelm Schlag|website=scholar.google.com|access-date=2019-05-03}}</ref> Schlag is one of the [[Editor-in-chief|managing editors]] of [[Inventiones Mathematicae]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inventiones mathematicae |url=https://www.springer.com/journal/222/editors |access-date=2023-09-15 |website=Springer |language=en |archive-date=2022-07-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220707225839/https://www.springer.com/journal/222/editors |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
* [[Sloan Research Fellow]], 2001
* [[Guggenheim Fellow]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/wilhelm-schlag/|title=Wilhelm Schlag|website=www.gf.org|access-date=2019-04-29}}</ref> 2009 
* Invited Speaker, [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], 2014
